Why Trust Us

Trust in this industry should be earned with evidence, not asserted in a banner. Here is exactly what sits behind every score we publish, and what you should check before believing any casino review — including ours.

We pay for our own accounts

Every review begins with a real account funded with our own ringgit, opened with ordinary Malaysian details through an ordinary Malaysian payment method. We do not accept press accounts, pre-loaded balances or VIP handling, because an account the operator knows is being watched does not behave like yours. When verification asks for documents, we send them and time how long the response takes.

Two people, not one

One team member writes the review. A second, named on the page alongside the author, independently repeats the critical checks — the licence lookup, the bonus arithmetic and at least one deposit and withdrawal cycle. If the two disagree, the review does not publish until the discrepancy is resolved. Both names and roles are listed on our editorial team page.

We time the whole payout, not the convenient part

"Instant withdrawal" usually describes the moment an operator approves a request, not the moment money reaches you. We record both: the timestamp we hit submit and the timestamp funds actually land, repeated across different days because weekend and public-holiday behaviour is where sites quietly differ. The figures in our reviews are what we measured, not what the operator advertises.

We verify licences at the register

A licence badge in a footer is an image, not a credential. We look the number up on the regulator's own register. Where a claim cannot be confirmed, we say so plainly and the score reflects it — that is precisely why Winbox sits at 7 out of 10 despite genuinely fast payouts, and why MB8's unverifiable claim costs it points.

We publish the bad news

Four of the fourteen casinos we currently cover score 5 out of 10. We still publish them in full, because knowing why a site ranks poorly is more useful than not finding it at all. Unresolved withdrawal complaints, thin corporate disclosure and licence claims we could not match to evidence all appear in the reviews rather than being edited out.

We tell you how we are paid

We earn affiliate commission when readers open accounts through our links, and we say so on every page carrying one. Commission rates play no part in ranking order. No operator previews a review, pays for placement or buys a score. Our about page sets out the funding model in full.

We date everything and correct in public

Every review carries a visible last-updated date and the names of both people involved. When bonus terms, banking limits or licensing change, we re-test and re-date rather than quietly amending the text. Corrections sent in by readers are verified and published the same way — the contact page explains how to report one.

What we do not claim

We cannot make an offshore casino safe, and we do not pretend otherwise. No site we cover holds a Malaysian licence, because none is issued for online casino play. We are not lawyers, nothing here is legal advice, and no bonus or strategy can guarantee a win. Our responsible gambling guide covers the risks honestly, and the method behind the numbers is in our editorial guidelines.
